articles.title: Mitchell Robinson Didn't Watch Knicks' NBA Title Ring Ceremony, Reacts to 1st Win vs. NY on Celtics
articles.summary: Boston Celtics center Mitchell Robinson revealed during an interview with NBA on Prime Video's Cassidy Hubbarth why he didn't watch the championship ring ceremony of his former team, the New York Knicks. In essence, it was for practical reasons.
articles.body:
Boston Celtics center Mitchell Robinson revealed during an interview with NBA on Prime Video's Cassidy Hubbarth why he didn't watch the championship ring ceremony of his former team, the New York Knicks. In essence, it was for practical reasons.

"I didn't have cable. We just came back from Detroit, and I don't have the channels on my phone and stuff like that," Robinson said.

When Hubbarth jokingly noted that this was part of the "moving process," Robinson agreed, with a smile.

In fairness to Robinson, watching the ceremony live may not have been convenient. The ceremony took place around 6:30-7 p.m. ET on Tuesday. Earlier in the afternoon, the Celtics visited Detroit for a 3 p.m. battle with the Pistons. The home team won, 121-113, and then the Celtics had to get ready and head back to Boston. In theory, Robinson could have perhaps multi-tasked, but he had business to attend to, ultimately.

Robinson played eight seasons on the Knicks and helped the team win the NBA title last year thanks to his strong rebounding, tenacious defense and infectious energy. He left in free agency for the C's, signing a three-year, $47.4 million contract.

It's clear there's still love between Robinson and the Knicks, as evidenced by the big man's comments that he still loves his old teammates. As Hubbarth noted, Knicks wing Josh Hart still saves Robinson's seat in film sessions.

Robinson faced his old Knicks team on Friday evening in Boston. The C's were victorious, 107-103, and Robinson started and played 22 minutes, posting four points, four rebounds, two assists and a block.

"They didn't want me?" Robinson said, per The Athletic's Fred Katz . "Yeah. That's what it felt like. … I was like, cool. There wasn't bad blood behind it. Man, fresh start."

Robinson added, per Katz, "The only thing that was kind of different was going to the rivals. But you know me, man. I like to troll. Nobody was happy with that move. But I was."

articles.title: El mejor Tatum está de vuelta y los campeones no levantan cabeza
articles.standfirst: Los Celtics ganan a los Knicks en un partido sin protagonismo de Hugo González
articles.summary: Los Celtics ganan a los Knicks en un partido sin protagonismo de Hugo González
articles.body: El día que Jayson Tatum se rompió el tendón de Aquiles (mayo de 2025), acabó el partido con 42 puntos ante los Knicks. Desde entonces comenzó un duro camino de vuelta que ha culminado un año y medio despúes de nuevo ante el equipo de Nueva York. Los 36 puntos anotados por Tatum ante los campeones en la victoria de su equipo, 107-103, representan su mejor partido desde su grave lesión y confirman que su mejor versión está de vuelta. Sobre todo porque 25 de esos 36 puntos los firmó en la segunda mitad y anotó siete de los últimos ocho puntos de su equipo para asegurar el primer triunfo de la temporada. Tatum además aportó nueve rebotes y siete asistencias acercándose al triple-doble, una suerte del juego que antes de su lesión dominaba. Para los Celtics es estrenar su casillero de victorias y hacerlo en el Garden ante uno de los candidatos a estar en las Finales de conferencia. Precisamente el arraque de los Knicks no ha podido ser peor, dos derrotas y sobre todo ante rivales directos por la supremacía del Este como Sixers y Celtics. Towns (22), Anunoby (20), un gran McBride desde el banquillo (20) y Brunson (19), no pudieron evitar la segunda decepción seguida del campeón, que no levanta cabeza. Es el primer campeón vigente que empiza la temporada 0-2 en 15 años, desde los Mavs de 2011-12. En los Celtics, con 15 de George y 15 de Queta, testimonial aportación de Hugo González con mucho menos protagonismo del esperado inicialmente: cuatro minutos, un sólo tiro fallado y una asistencia. Fue el jugador del banquillo con menos impacto en los Celtics. Aunque la victoria y su actuación fueron importantes para Tatum, los periodistas en la rueda de prensa posterior quisieron saber algo más de su relación con Jaylen Brown y el cruce de mensajes en las redes. Brown publicó una gorra ('cap' en inglés) tras un vídeo de Tatum en el que decía estar tan sorprendido como el retso del mundo por el traspaso de su compañero en pretemporada. "Este no es el jodido caso de Shaq y Kobe", dijo Tatum, refiriéndose a los problemas que tuvieron Shaquille O'Neal y el fallecido Kobe Bryant en los Lakers que acabó destruyendo la pareja. "No hay ningún conflicto; no se trata de eso. Debería haber más elogios. Entiendo que el drama genera clics y visitas, pero no va conmigo. No culpo a nadie por cómo se siente; cada uno tiene derecho a sus propios sentimientos y todos pasamos por situaciones distintas en nuestras vidas". Tatum se explicó luego: "Me puse en contacto con él el día en que fue traspasado. Lo llamé, le envié mensajes. Entiendo que cada persona procesa las cosas de manera distinta. A estas alturas de nuestras vidas, ya somos demasiado mayores para que nuestra relación sea objeto de debate en internet. Si hay algo que hablar, sin duda podemos tener esa conversación".

articles.title: Kessler y Reaves minimizan el récord negativo de Doncic
articles.standfirst: Segunda victoria en dos partidos de los Lakers esta temporada
articles.summary: Segunda victoria en dos partidos de los Lakers esta temporada
articles.body: Dos jugadores protagonistas en la pretemporada dieron la cara por los Lakers ante los Clippers (125-117) en lo que fue la segunda victoria de la temporada para los amarillos en dos partidos, ambos jugador en el crypto.com Arena. Austin Reaves, el jugador al que los Lakers querían trespasar pero no lo hicieron ante la oposición de Luka Doncic, fue el mejor con 28 puntos y nueve asistencias y sobre todo desatascando el ataque local ante el mal día de su líder. Mientras, Walker Kessler, el jugador que vino traspasado de los Jazz como la pieza crucial en el juego interior angelino, anotó 22 puntos y puso seis tapones. Es la primera vez en cinco temporadas que Kessler encadena dos noches con 20 o más puntos en la NBA. Y lo ha hecho en sus dos primeros partidos en L.A. Los dos más Doncic, autor de 23 puntos, acabaron con la resistencia de los Clippers, que presentaron batalla con los 26 de Darius Garland, los 22 de Brook Lopez y los 16 de Rui Hachimura en su primer regreso a la que fue su casa durante algo más de tres temporadas y media. En el 'hermano pobre' de L.A. no jugó un sólo segundo el español Baba Miller después de su buen estreno ante los Kings. Kessler y Reaves salvaron la cara de los Lakers en un día aciago para Doncic. El esloveno estuvo mal en el tiro, 8/21 en tiros de campo con 2/8 en triples, pero horrible en la dirección. Perdió 11 balones lo que ya es un récord personal negativo en la NBA. Doncic se quedó a tres de los 14 que tiene como tope absoluto John Drew desde 1978. Pero hay que insistir, estamos hablando de un récord negativo. De hecho el técnico de los Lakers JJ Redick trató de explicar esas 11 pérdidas de su jugador: "Le hicieron muchas veces un dos contra uno. Los rivales intensificaron la presión y buscaron forzar pérdidas de balón a partir de eso, así que continuaremos construyendo nuestras opciones para manejarlo mejor", dijo. A pesar de sus pérdidas, Doncic se mostró contento al final del partido. Primero por la actuación de Kessler. "Sabemos lo que podemos esperar de él. No me sorprende cómo está jugando, sabe cómo jugar a este deporte", y después con las dos victorias de su equipo: "Aún tenemos mucho margen de mejora, pero sin duda hemos evolucionado".

articles.title: La defensa de los Heat arruina el fabuloso arranque de Antetokounmpo
articles.standfirst: El griego firma el mejor arranque anotador de su carrera... pero el peor en lo colectivo
articles.summary: El griego firma el mejor arranque anotador de su carrera... pero el peor en lo colectivo
articles.body: Nunca, en toda la historia de los Miami Heat, un jugador había arrancado con 71 puntos anotados en los dos primeros partidos de la temporada. El mejor había sido LeBron James, que sumó 63 en sus dos primeros partidos de la temporada 2011-2012 en la que los Heat, por cierto, fueron campeones. Giannis Antetokounmpo suma dos actuaciones formidables: le metió 35 puntos a Minnesota y lo mejoró poco después con los 36 ante los Pistons. Un promedio de 35,5 puntos por noche. Pero dos derrotas, la última ante Detroit en Miami, 111-128. Para el griego, es su mejor arranque de carrera, nunca había comenzado tan bien en el aspecto ofensivo. Pero nunca había comenzado tan mal en lo colectivo. Es la primera vez que Giannis pierde sus dos primeros partidos de la temporada. Durante su estancia en los Bucks a Milwaukee sólo le pasó eso una vez, 2015-16, pero Giannis se perdió uno de esos dos partidos. El contrapunto al juego ofensivo de Anteto es la fragilidad defensiva de los Heat que acumulan otro dato histórico negativo. Nunca los Heat habían comenzado la temporada encajando 259 puntos en dos partidos (131 ante los Wolves y 128 ante los Pistons). Sumando las desventajas de los dos partidos, Miami perdió por 42 puntos. "Queríamos que las cosas salieran bien, no solo por él, sino también por nosotros", dijo al final del partido el entrenador de los Heat, Erik Spoelstra. "A Giannis realmente le importa. Quiere que esto funcione. Sus compañeros también desean de verdad que esto funcione. Lo lograremos. Simplemente no está ocurriendo según nuestros plazos actuales; no es exactamente como queríamos empezar la temporada", explica. Los Heat se midieron, eso sí, a un equipo que ha comenzado en forma. Los Pistons ganaron a los Celtics en el arranque y en Miami, mandando un interesante mensaje a los que no piensan que pueden volver a estar en lo más alto de la conferencia. John Collins (23), Duncan Robinson (17 con 5/10 en triples) y Cade Cunningham (18 y ocho asistencias), fueron los mejores para unos Pistons que empiezan 2-0 una temporada por primera vez desde 2018-19.

articles.title: Luka's 'Not Michael Jordan,' Yaxel Lendeborg Addresses Trash Talk in Video, 'I'm Not Afraid'
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg isn't backing down from his comments about Luka Dončić after the Los Angeles Lakers' season-opening victory on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg isn't backing down from his comments about Luka Dončić after the Los Angeles Lakers' season-opening victory on Wednesday.

After the Warriors' loss to the Memphis Grizzlies on Friday, Lendeborg doubled down when he told reporters "I'm not afraid" of anyone and Dončić is "not Michael Jordan."

Lendeborg and Dončić were going at it both verbally and physically in Wednesday's game. One moment saw Dončić calling Lendeborg "24 and a rookie" and he needs to "relax."

Things got chippy enough between the two that Lendeborg at one point was called for a technical foul late in the second quarter. He said after the game that Dončić "sucks" and he "lost all respect" for the Lakers star because he was "complaining the entire game."

Despite the boldness of a rookie after his first game so publicly criticizing a superstar player, Warriors head coach Steve Kerr did appreciate Lendeborg's approach while offering one critique.

"I love it," Kerr said. "I think the bravado, not backing down, it's great. ... Hell yeah, but don't foul him next time … back up your words."

Dončić got the last laugh in the game with 28 points, eight rebounds and seven assists to lead the Lakers to a 127-105 victory.

Adding more insult to the situation for Lendeborg is the Warriors blew a 12-point lead in the fourth quarter against the Grizzlies on Friday night to fall to 0-2 for the first time since the 2020-21 season.

Lendeborg showed up for Golden State with 18 points, 13 rebounds, six assists and three steals in 37 minutes. He will try to help the Warriors get their first win of the season on Saturday when they take on the Phoenix Suns at Mortgage Matchup Center.

articles.title: Knicks & Spurs on Wrong Side of History with Rare Stat, What Did Brunson & Wemby Say After Losses?
articles.summary: Four months after meeting in the NBA Finals, the New York Knicks and San Antonio Spurs find themselves on the wrong side of history to start the 2026-27 season with both teams sitting at 0-2 after their first two games.
articles.body:
Four months after meeting in the NBA Finals, the New York Knicks and San Antonio Spurs find themselves on the wrong side of history to start the 2026-27 season with both teams sitting at 0-2 after their first two games.

Per ESPN Insights, this marks the third time in NBA history that the two reigning conference champions lost their first two games the next season.

Overreacting to every NBA team's first game

The Knicks fell to 0-2 with a 107-103 loss to the Boston Celtics at TD Garden. The Spurs lost 114-110 to the Houston Rockets on Friday, dropping each off their first two games at home after going 32-8 at Frost Bank Center last season.

Coming out of the Knicks' loss against Boston, Jalen Brunson was able to find some positive takeaways from their performance relative to how they played in Tuesday's opener against the Philadelphia 76ers.

"I think we took a stride, just not big enough strides," Brunson told reporters . "There's positives and negatives to take from this game. We know what we have to do, and the things I think are glaring to us are controllable. So that's a positive we can take from this."

The Spurs' loss was highlighted by Victor Wembanyama's last-second layup that would have tied the game being blocked by Amen Thompson.

Wembanyama admitted afterward that he "would have dunked the ball" instead of going for a layup if he could do that sequence over again.

One thing Wembanyama responded to was a question about closing the game with the three-guard lineup featuring Dylan Harper, Stephon Castle and De'Aaron Fox rather than going with more three-point shooting by keeping at least one of Julian Champagnie or Devin Vassell on the floor.

"I feel like we're comfortable with it," said Wembanyama. "We've finished games with this lineup before and in the playoffs as well. It's not a concern for us."

Other Spurs players offered their assessment of what's gone wrong for the team thus far. Fox attributed it to them having a poor preseason and not being able to sneak up on teams like they did last season:

"I think, starting off, our preseason was s--tty. That's what happened, and we can't try to be a team that's just trying to flip a switch. ... We knew coming into this league that we weren't surprising anybody. I think last year, when we started off 8-0, it was a surprise to people. So coming into this year, I don't think anything that we will do will surprise anybody, and we've seen that already."

Dylan Harper cited "lapses on defense" as an issue they need to correct.

"I feel like we have a lot of lapses on defense," Harper said. "I raise my hand to that, and I feel like I and the team. We all got to get better."

Harper did note they still have 80 games remaining, so there's no panic setting in right now: "It's not going to be perfect from Day 1."

Among the key stats from the slow start for both teams is New York's offense and San Antonio's defense. The Knicks had the fourth-best offense by rating last season; the Spurs were third in defensive rating.

Through two games this season, the Knicks rank 20th on offense and the Spurs are 17th on defense.

It's still very early to have any big takeaways, but the slow starts for two teams that were expected to be among the best in the NBA does open the door for others to take advantage while they search for answers.

articles.title: 'What the F--k is Wrong with Him,' Kevin Durant Reacts to Wemby Getting Blocked by Amen on Video
articles.summary: Kevin Durant questioned Victor Wembanyama's decision to try going for a layup over Amen Thompson in the final seconds of the Houston Rockets' 114-110 victory over the San Antonio Spurs on Friday night.
articles.body:
Kevin Durant questioned Victor Wembanyama's decision to try going for a layup over Amen Thompson in the final seconds of the Houston Rockets' 114-110 victory over the San Antonio Spurs on Friday night.

Durant told reporters after the win his reaction in the moment was "what the f--k is wrong with him" as Wembanyama tried to go for a layup with Thompson guarding him.

"I said, 'What the f--- is wrong with him, thinking he was just going to lay it up so easily?'" Durant said.

The Spurs were trailing 112-110 when they got the ball back with five seconds remaining coming out of a timeout. Wembanyama caught a pass in the post and turned to go for a layup, but Thompson met him in the air and got a hand on the ball despite the significant size difference between the two.

"I just knew they were going to try to get probably me or one of the other smaller guys on him," Thompson said of his game-saving play. "I jump pretty high, so I wouldn't try to keep ducking [in on] me."

Even though Thompson's offensive game has improved since he entered the NBA, his defense remains his primary calling card. He has finished top 10 in Defensive Player of the Year voting in each of the past two seasons and made the All-Defensive first team in 2024-25.

That defensive aptitude from Thompson was on full display in this moment. It was one of two blocks he had in this game, in addition to having 20 points, 10 rebounds and four assists.

With Fred VanVleet back for the Rockets after missing all of last season due to a torn ACL, Thompson no longer has to run point for the offense. Easing some of that burden on him could help him reach another level on defense.

If that ends up being the case, the Rockets could put themselves in the mix with the top-tier teams in the Western Conference as this season goes on.

articles.title: Wemby Reacts to Amen's Block, Says What He'd Do Differently in New Video After Spurs Lose to Rockets
articles.summary: Victor Wembanyama knows what he did wrong on the final offensive possession that resulted in his potential game-tying shot being blocked by Amen Thompson in the San Antonio Spurs' 114-110 loss to the Houston Rockets on Friday night.
articles.body:
Victor Wembanyama knows what he did wrong on the final offensive possession that resulted in his potential game-tying shot being blocked by Amen Thompson in the San Antonio Spurs' 114-110 loss to the Houston Rockets on Friday night.

Asked what he would have done differently during his postgame press conference (starts at :10 mark), Wembanyama said "I would have dunked the ball."

The Spurs were trailing by two with five seconds remaining and possession of the ball. Wembanyama caught a pass in the paint and made a move to the basket, but he was met in midair by Thompson, who blocked the layup attempt.

Given the size difference between the 7'4" Wembanyama and 6'7" Thompson, it was a surprise to see the Rockets forward match him when they got in the air.

Thompson had great position to keep Wembanyama from getting as close to the basket needed for an easy dunk attempt, but the Spurs star has such long arms that it wasn't impossible for him to try for a slam rather than a finger roll.

It could also be argued if Wembanyama had tried for a dunk and generated contact with Thompson, he might have been able to draw a foul to at least get two free-throw attempts that could have tied the game.

Instead, Wembanyama and the Spurs are searching for answers amid an 0-2 start to the season. This marks the first time they have lost back-to-back games in the regular season since Jan. 11-13 last season.

San Antonio will look to get in the win column for the first time in the 2026-27 season on Saturday against the Dallas Mavericks at American Airlines Center.

articles.title: Warriors HC Kerr Calls Out Grizzlies for 'Flopping,' Says NBA Refs 'Bought Into It' in Viral Video
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr called out the officiating following his team's 111-108 home loss to the Memphis Grizzlies on Friday.
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr called out the officiating following his team's 111-108 home loss to the Memphis Grizzlies on Friday.

Speaking to reporters after the game, Kerr said, "All of the flopping that was going on, every time somebody ran into a screen, they just went down, and the refs bought into it."

Golden State held a six-point lead entering the fourth quarter, but it was outscored 27-18 by Memphis in the final frame, resulting in the Warriors falling to 0-2 during the early going of the 2026-27 season.

All signs pointed toward the Warriors cruising to a win when they led by 12 with 3:47 remaining, however, the Grizzlies mounted a furious comeback.

Memphis went on a 17-0 run to take the lead and ultimately win the game, although a critical call in the closing seconds aided them.

After the Grizzlies took a 108-106 lead, the Warriors drew up a play for Stephen Curry to potentially make the go-ahead three-pointer, but Draymond Green was called for an illegal screen with 12.8 seconds remaining.

A furious Kerr argued the call and got hit with a technical foul, which gave Memphis a free throw and possession of the ball.

The Grizzlies made their technical free throw and converted a two-point basket on the ensuing possession to seal the victory.

While it is fair to debate the validity of Green's offensive foul, the fact that the Grizzlies were able to overcome such a massive deficit speaks to an even bigger issue.

Of course, it is still early in the season and the Warriors are without two key players in the injured Jimmy Butler and ill Kristaps Porziņģis, but Golden State needs to win games and remain in the playoff race while they are out.

The challenge for Kerr now is to rally the troops and ensure that Friday's loss doesn't snowball into bigger issues, as the Warriors are set to embark on a three-game road trip that starts with the Phoenix Suns on Saturday night.

articles.title: LeBron James' $15 million Polymarket deal raises eyebrows as his reported endorsement earnings outpace his 76ers paycheck by millions
articles.summary: LeBron James has spent more than two decades building a basketball career that few athletes can match.
articles.body: LeBron James has spent more than two decades building a basketball career that few athletes can match. Yet his latest business move has created an unusual financial comparison. The Philadelphia 76ers star is reportedly set to earn $15 million annually from Polymarket, nearly four times his expected NBA salary for the 2026-27 season. The deal comes as prediction markets attract growing attention and face questions about their role in sports. For James, the agreement highlights the earning power of his global reputation. It also puts the relationship between professional athletes, lucrative endorsements and emerging financial platforms under a brighter spotlight.LeBron James' $15 million Polymarket deal puts his NBA salary in perspectiveThe figures behind James' latest partnership have caught the attention of sports business observers. According to Front Office Sports, Polymarket will pay the basketball star $15 million a year under an endorsement agreement. The report, published on September 16, cited sources familiar with the arrangement.That amount stands well above his expected earnings from Philadelphia. James signed a two-year contract worth $8 million with the 76ers in July. His salary for the 2026-27 season is approximately $3.9 million, meaning the reported Polymarket payment is almost four times his basketball income for the same period.The difference becomes even clearer when comparing the two figures directly. His reported annual endorsement payment exceeds his 76ers salary by about $11.1 million. That is a striking contrast for a player whose reputation rests on his performance on the court.However, the comparison does not mean James has abandoned basketball as his main professional pursuit. An NBA salary reflects a player's contract with a team, while endorsement income comes from commercial agreements. Each serves a different purpose, and neither figure alone captures an athlete's total earnings.The reported deal also shows how valuable James remains to major brands. Even late in his playing career, his name can attract attention well beyond basketball. Companies can use that reach to connect with audiences who follow sports, entertainment and popular culture.What LeBron James will do under his Polymarket partnershipJames is reportedly joining Polymarket as a paid endorser, not as an investor. Front Office Sports reported that the agreement involves several promotional commitments, including social media posts and other content. The exact length of the deal has not been disclosed publicly.The campaign will focus on football rather than basketball. That distinction matters because James is an active NBA player, and promoting markets tied to the sport in which he competes could create additional concerns around conflicts of interest and public trust.Polymarket is a prediction-market platform where users trade contracts linked to the likelihood of future events. These markets can cover politics, economics, entertainment and sports. The company has become part of a wider contest among prediction platforms seeking new customers and greater visibility.James first teased the partnership in a social media video in September, prompting interest from fans before reports revealed the deal's reported value. Other well-known names, including former New York Yankees star Derek Jeter and retired NFL quarterback Eli Manning, also appeared in Polymarket's promotional campaign. Sources told Front Office Sports that their endorsement arrangements were smaller than James' deal.For James, the arrangement adds another commercial relationship to an already extensive portfolio. His appeal reaches across sports and entertainment, giving brands access to a broad audience. Still, the reported $15 million figure remains based on media reporting rather than a publicly released contract.Why LeBron James' Polymarket deal is attracting scrutinyThe financial value is only one part of the story. The partnership arrives at a time when prediction markets are facing difficult questions about their influence on sports and public events.Polymarket allows users to trade contracts linked to the outcomes of future events. Supporters see these markets as a way to measure public expectations, while critics question whether some contracts create ethical concerns or encourage people to treat sensitive events as opportunities to make money.Those concerns have intensified following a recent controversy involving a market on whether any of seven men accused of sexually assaulting or exploiting a Cornell University student would face felony charges. The men have denied the allegations or disputed their involvement. Polymarket removed the contract after it attracted more than $450,000 in trading volume and drew widespread criticism.The incident also put the company's celebrity endorsers under the spotlight. According to the Associated Press, an advocacy group launched a petition calling on prominent figures, including James, to cut ties with Polymarket. Critics questioned the decision to associate celebrity names with a platform that had hosted such a market.Polymarket defended its decision to remove the contract, with a spokesperson saying: “Our primary goal at Polymarket is to bring objective, data-driven insight to the most important questions of our time. This market addressed whether the government would take action — a process that deserves scrutiny, particularly in a case of such serious concern. That said, we believe in the wisdom of crowds, have heard them loud and clear, and removed the market.”The controversy does not establish that James was involved in creating or managing the disputed market. Nor does the available reporting show that he had any role in the events behind it. The criticism instead concerns his decision to promote a company that operates in a sector facing growing public scrutiny.For an athlete with a global following, that distinction matters. A commercial partnership can attract attention to a brand, but it can also expose the endorser to questions about the company's business practices.LeBron James' business empire extends beyond basketballThe Polymarket agreement fits into a broader picture of James' financial success. Over the years, he has built a portfolio that extends beyond his NBA salary, using endorsements, media projects and investments to create income outside basketball.His reported Polymarket earnings are particularly striking because his playing salary has fallen sharply from the amount he earned with the Los Angeles Lakers during the previous season. James signed with Philadelphia on a two-year, $8 million contract, a move that gives the team greater flexibility while he continues his career.His commercial value, meanwhile, remains substantial. James has worked with major brands throughout his career, and his long-running relationship with Nike is one of the most prominent examples of an athlete building lasting business ties. His media ventures and investments have also helped him establish a presence beyond the court.That wider portfolio explains why his latest endorsement has attracted so much attention. The reported $15 million annual payment is not simply another sponsorship figure. It highlights how a famous athlete can earn more from a commercial partnership than from an entire season of professional competition.Still, the reported value should not be mistaken for a complete picture of James' income. The public does not have the full Polymarket contract, its precise duration or every condition attached to the agreement. The $15 million figure comes from reporting by Front Office Sports, which cited unnamed sources familiar with the deal.What the Polymarket deal means for LeBron JamesJames' partnership illustrates a growing challenge for modern sports stars. Their commercial influence can be enormous, but the companies they choose to represent may operate in industries that attract debate over regulation, ethics and public trust.The financial contrast is clear. Polymarket is reportedly paying James about $15 million annually, while the 76ers will pay him roughly $3.9 million for the 2026-27 season. That is a difference of more than $11 million, with the endorsement worth almost four times his expected NBA salary.Yet the broader question is not simply how much James stands to earn. It is how celebrity partnerships affect the public perception of prediction markets as those platforms seek a larger role in sports culture.For now, the reported agreement remains an endorsement deal, not an ownership stake. Its full terms have not been disclosed, and there is no evidence in the available reporting that James was involved in the controversial Cornell market.The deal nevertheless places two powerful forces side by side: James' enduring commercial appeal and the growing debate around prediction markets. His earnings comparison with the 76ers makes an immediate headline, but the questions surrounding the partnership may prove more significant over time.As prediction platforms continue to expand, athletes and companies alike will face greater attention over the brands they promote. For James, the reported $15 million agreement is another example of his earning power. articles.title: Knicks' Karl-Anthony Towns gets major contract extension timeline update after being disappointed
articles.summary: Even though Karl-Anthony Towns didn't get a contract extension before the regular season. It seems like there is a sense of when one can come.
articles.body:
The New York Knicks have started the season 0-2 after winning the NBA Finals just a few months ago. It isn't the start the team wanted, but with 80 games left to play, there is no reason to panic just yet.

Before the season started, the organization attempted to extend Karl-Anthony Towns and Josh Hart. However, the Knicks shut down those discussions to focus on the regular season and limit distractions.

"As an organization, our entire focus is on preparing for the upcoming season and delivering another year for our fans to be proud of. As a result, we will not be negotiating contract extensions until later in the season and will remain solely focused on preparing for the start of the season," a Knicks spokesperson told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Although the decision was intended to limit distractions, the attention surrounding the situation may have made matters worse. Towns expressed disappointment when asked about the Knicks' decision to halt extension talks.

"It was news to me. Very disappointed to say the least. Let's state the obvious. It's business, but there is business on the court for us to handle," Towns said.

While no deal was reached during the offseason, there now appears to be a clearer idea of Towns' asking price and a potential timeline for when both sides could reach an agreement.

"The word on the street over the last few weeks is that Towns wants something in the $225-240 million range on a four-year extension… When asked about not receiving an extension, Towns was upset, but he made it clear that it is just business… Many around the NBA anticipate the Knicks and Towns agreeing to a new extension sometime in the middle of the 2026-27 season," NBA insider Brett Siegel wrote.

For Towns, it should be encouraging to know that an extension could still be on the table, even if an agreement does not come until the middle of the season. Once a deal is finalized, the center can focus entirely on basketball without the uncertainty surrounding his contract.

The Knicks are looking to get into the win column after their slow start, and resolving the contract situation could help provide some clarity moving forward. If the two sides reach an agreement midway through the season, Towns would have greater certainty about his future in New York.

articles.title: ‘An unfortunate mistake’: Knicks admit error in using championship rings as phishing bait
articles.summary: The New York Knicks’ parent company says it is giving out more than $3.7 million worth of championship rings and jewelry after acknowledging an “unfortunate mistake” of using an offer of free rings to lure employees into a cybersecurity test. As first reported by The Athletic, the email said employees were eligible for a free Knicks championship ring.
articles.body: The New York Knicks’ parent company says it is giving out more than $3.7 million worth of championship rings and jewelry after acknowledging an “unfortunate mistake” of using an offer of free rings to lure employees into a cybersecurity test. As first reported by The Athletic, the email said employees were eligible for a free Knicks championship ring. Instead, clicking on the offer earned them a mandatory cybersecurity training, the outlet reported. “The company had previously sent out an email to its corporate team as a simulation of a phishing attack designed to strengthen our security against hackers,” Madison Square Garden Sports said in a statement. “MSG was recently hacked and extorted using an employee login and password obtained through a similar phishing attack.” The company said it is giving players, coaches, employees and others in the Knicks organization more than 275 rings and pieces of jewelry worth more than $3.7 million. NFL Network host Rich Eisen criticized Knicks owner James L. Dolan over the email on his show, saying: “The man is phishing his own employees with a bait of a championship ring. Can you be any worse of an employer? Can you be any lower than that?” The Athletic also reported that Knicks assistant coaches were handed empty boxes during the ring ceremony ahead of the Knicks’ first game of the season on Tuesday. The assistants had been told earlier that day they would not receive their rings that evening but would get them eventually, according to the outlet.

articles.title: Kawhi Leonard Addresses NBA Investigation After $700K Fine, 'I Know What Type of Guy I Was'
articles.summary: Toronto Raptors star Kawhi Leonard spoke Friday about the salary cap circumvention investigation that resulted in him incurring a hefty fine and ultimately getting traded from the Los Angeles Clippers this past offseason.
articles.body:
Toronto Raptors star Kawhi Leonard spoke Friday about the salary cap circumvention investigation that resulted in him incurring a hefty fine and ultimately getting traded from the Los Angeles Clippers this past offseason.

In an interview with David Aldridge of The Athletic, Leonard discussed the NBA investigation and end result, saying, "It was a long summer. It was kind of expected. I didn't know when it was going to happen. But they made their decision when they did. I just stayed focused. I know what type of guy I was. I was honest. And that's all you can do, be honest; just look in the mirror yourself and see if you did anything wrong. Just kept moving forward. Talked to God, my family. I just kept moving forward after that."

In September, the NBA announced that its investigation determined the Clippers were guilty of salary cap circumvention due to team governor Steve Ballmer facilitating a $28 million endorsement deal between Leonard and Aspiration.

The Clippers were fined $30 million and docked five future first-round draft picks, while Ballmer was banned from partaking in all team and league activities for a year.

Leonard was fined $700,000 for his role, but he was not suspended, and the previously-agreed-upon trade to send him to Toronto was executed once the investigation concluded.

Now, the 35-year-old Leonard is back for his second tour of duty with the Raptors after leading them to their first and only NBA championship back in 2019.

The seven-time All-Star and two-time NBA Finals MVP suggested to Aldridge that his main goal now is to aid in the development of the Raptors' younger players.

"That [winning another championship] would top off the career, obviously," Leonard said. "But more than that, I just want to help these guys get their mindset together. They've still got a lot of years to play. I just want to leave the stamp with them, just help them get better for when their time comes. They're still 23, 24, 25. Three or four years from now, they're going to still be in their prime. I might not be here. So that's all I want to do, help the team, help the organization. Whether that's winning one, or just helping them carry that over and win one themselves, that's all I want to do."

Leonard has helped the Raptors to a 2-0 start, and he continues to play at a high level despite having been in the NBA since 2011.

Last season, Leonard was named an All-Star and Second Team All-NBA selection, while finishing seventh in the NBA MVP voting.

If he provides similar results this season in Toronto, the Raptors should be legitimate threats to represent the Eastern Conference in the NBA Finals.

articles.title: Malik Beasley reportedly plans to plead guilty in federal NBA gambling case
articles.summary: Former NBA guard Malik Beasley is reportedly negotiating a plea agreement with federal prosecutors over charges stemming from an alleged gambling scheme invo...
articles.body:
According to The Athletic's Mike Vorkunov on Saturday, Beasley is in discussions with Department of Justice attorneys after court records filed Friday indicated that he intends to change his initial not guilty plea.

However, Beasley's attorney, Steve Haney, clarified that the 29-year-old has not officially decided to plead guilty. Haney confirmed that discussions with prosecutors from the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of New York remain ongoing, with a final decision expected early next week.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Federal prosecutors indicted Beasley in June, alleging that he intentionally manipulated his performances in multiple games to benefit gamblers who placed wagers on his individual statistics.

The indictment identified games against the Cleveland Cavaliers on Jan. 26, 2024, Charlotte Hornets on Feb. 27, Los Angeles Clippers on March 10 and Brooklyn Nets on March 21 as part of the alleged scheme.

Prosecutors also accused former NBA player Ed Davis of participating in the operation . According to the indictment, Beasley accumulated millions of dollars in gambling debt before receiving a loan from Davis, his former Minnesota Timberwolves teammate.

"Only way you can beat Vegas is sports betting," Davis allegedly texted Beasley in December 2023. "Everything else, they got the edge."

Davis and Beasley's former agent, Paolo Zamorano, have pleaded not guilty.

Meanwhile, two additional defendants, Robert Gorodetsky and Ernesto Plascencia, intend to change their pleas to guilty. Another defendant, William Brown, previously pleaded guilty.

Malik Beasley's gambling case adds to growing NBA investigation

Beasley's legal troubles have overshadowed a productive nine-year NBA career that included stops with the Denver Nuggets, Timberwolves, Utah Jazz, Los Angeles Lakers, Bucks and Detroit Pistons .

The former first-round pick earned nearly $60 million in NBA salaries and appeared positioned to secure another lucrative contract following his impressive 2024-25 campaign with Detroit.

Beasley averaged 16.3 points while shooting 41.6% from 3-point range, finishing second in NBA Sixth Man of the Year voting. However, the Pistons reportedly withdrew a three-year, $42 million contract offer after learning about the federal investigation.

His case is among several federal investigations involving alleged gambling-related misconduct across the league.

Former NBA center Jontay Porter pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit wire fraud in 2024 after admitting his involvement in a scheme to manipulate his performances. The NBA subsequently banned him for life.

Former player Damon Jones also pleaded guilty this spring to charges involving gambling-related schemes, including allegations that he provided confidential information to bettors.

Miami Heat guard Terry Rozier has pleaded not guilty to separate allegations that he accepted a bribe to remove himself from a Charlotte Hornets game to benefit gamblers.

Former Portland Trail Blazers coach Chauncey Billups faces separate charges involving an alleged rigged poker operation. He has pleaded not guilty.

For Beasley, the ongoing negotiations represent a potentially significant development in a federal case that has left his NBA future uncertain.

articles.title: Paolo Banchero Injured, Latest NBA Rumors on Magic Star's Timeline to Return from Ankle Injury
articles.summary: Things are going from bad to worse for the Orlando Magic amid an 0-2 start with Paolo Banchero likely to miss multiple weeks after leaving Friday's loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves early due to a right ankle injury.
articles.body:
Things are going from bad to worse for the Orlando Magic amid an 0-2 start with Paolo Banchero likely to miss multiple weeks after leaving Friday's loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves early due to a right ankle injury.

Per ESPN's Shams Charania , Banchero has been diagnosed with a low-grade high-ankle sprain that typically carries a four-to-six week recovery timeline.

Banchero appeared to tweak his ankle early in the third quarter when he collided with Jalen Suggs going for a rebound. He went to the locker room and did not return.

This marks the second time in the last three seasons that Banchero has suffered a significant injury early in the year. He suffered a torn oblique in the fifth game of the 2024-25 season and missed more than two months.

The ankle injury may not keep Banchero out for that long, but it does leave the Magic once again in a difficult spot as they try to replace his production.

Orlando was held to 93 points against the Timberwolves on Friday night. It was the fifth-lowest scoring game by a team in the still-early 2026-27 season.

Banchero leads the Magic in scoring average (24.5 points per game), assists (7.5) and shot 69.6 percent from the field through the first two games. His absence will put more of the onus on Franz Wagner and Desmond Bane for offense.

Tristan Da Silva will likely move into Banchero's spot in the starting lineup. The third-year forward is off to a slow start, but he shot 37.4 percent from three-point range on 4.2 attempts per game in 77 appearances last season.

The Magic are off on Saturday before beginning a three-game road trip on Sunday against the defending NBA champion New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark, A'ja Wilson, Angel Reese Headline 2026 All-WNBA Teams
articles.summary: Ten WNBA players were celebrated Saturday with the announcement of this 2026 All-WNBA teams.
articles.body:
Ten WNBA players were celebrated Saturday with the announcement of this 2026 All-WNBA teams.

This year's All-WNBA First Team featured the Indiana Fever's Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell as well as the Minnesota Lynx's Olivia Miles, New York Liberty's Breanna Stewart and Las Vegas Aces' A'ja Wilson.

The Second Team was led by the Atlanta Dream's Angel Reese and Rhyne Howard alongside the Washington Mystics' Shakira Austin, Dallas Wings' Paige Bueckers and Aces' Jackie Young.

The news comes as Reese and Howard prepare to continue fighting for a WNBA title when the Dream tip off Game 4 of the 2026 WNBA Finals Saturday at 1 p.m. ET against the visiting Golden State Valkyries.

The Valkyries are the fourth team to make the WNBA Finals without any players having earned an All-WNBA nod, per The IX Sports' Drake Keeler . The news comes after Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase finished second in WNBA Coach of the Year voting.

Keeler noted that none of the other three teams without an All-WNBA player on the roster won the title after the snub. The Dream are heading into Game 4 with a 2-1 series lead over the Valkyries.

The only first-time First-Team member this year is Miles, who was named the WNBA's Rookie of the Year after surpassing Clark's first-year record for total points.

Clark and Mitchell each earned their second First-Team nod, while Wilson and Stewart were celebrated with the honor for the sixth and seventh times, respectively.

Wilson earned her latest All-WNBA nod after becoming the first player in WNBA history to win three straight MVP awards.

Reese followed up her Defensive Player of the Year honor with her first All-WNBA nod. She was one of five players including Austin, Howard, Wilson and Stewart to earn the All-WNBA nod after being named to this year's WNBA All-Defensive Teams.

The Dream star was joined as a first-time nominee by Howard and Austin, while Bueckers earned her second appearance on the Second-Team list and Young made her third.

Bueckers is now the first player since Tina Charles to open her WNBA career with consecutive All-WNBA nods, per Myah Taylor of the Dallas Morning News.

articles.title: Magic's Paolo Banchero suffers high ankle sprain in loss to Timberwolves, reportedly could be out 4-6 weeks
articles.summary: Banchero left Friday night's loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves early.
articles.body:
The Orlando Magic need a spell to lift their injury curse. They've been haunted by ailments, the latest of which reportedly could sideline their best player for more than a month.

Magic star Paolo Banchero is now nursing a low-grade right high ankle sprain, the team announced Saturday . The injury, according to ESPN's Shams Charania , usually comes with a four-to-six-week recovery timeline.

Banchero, a 23-year-old one-time All-Star forward, exited a 115-93 loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves in the third quarter Friday night and didn't return. Banchero sustained the injury in the first half, per the team.

He finished with 14 points, 6 rebounds and 5 assists in a setback that dropped the Magic to 0-2 in the infancy of Sean Sweeney's first season at the helm .

During the Magic's season-opening defeat to the Atlanta Hawks, Banchero piled up 35 points on 10-of-12 shooting, plus 10 assists and 7 rebounds.

The Duke product, whom Orlando selected No. 1 overall in the 2022 draft, is coming off a 2025-26 campaign that saw him average 22.2 points, 8.4 rebounds and 5.2 assists per game. He helped the Magic reach the playoffs for the third consecutive season, except they were once again bounced in the first round.

Orlando blew a 3-1 lead to the top-seeded Detroit Pistons, leading to the firing of Jamahl Mosley, who's now the head coach of the New Orleans Pelicans.

Just before that coaching change, in the fallout of the Magic's collapse, Banchero admitted his group wasn't "good enough" at the time to make the Eastern Conference finals or NBA Finals.

Due to the Magic's injury woes, it's been difficult for them to realize their potential. Now, just two games into Sweeney's stint, Banchero is sidelined.

Last season, Banchero, Franz Wagner, Jalen Suggs, Desmond Bane and Wendell Carter Jr. were all on the floor together for just 182 minutes, according to ESPN , which also reported that, during that small sample size, the Magic outscored opponents by 45 points.

Banchero missed 36 games in 2024-25. Suggs wasn't on the court for 47 games that season. Wagner was out for 48 games last season and then notably wasn't available for the final three games of the first-round series versus the Pistons .

articles.title: Cooper Flagg sustains mild shoulder sprain in win over Pacers after taking hard foul from Aaron Nesmith
articles.summary: Nesmith was called for a flagrant foul for the contact; he was also given a technical after the collision sparked a heated argument with Naji Marshall.
articles.body:
Cooper Flagg suffered a mild left shoulder sprain during a 121-105 win over the Indiana Pacers on Friday, the Dallas Mavericks announced Saturday .

Flagg will be out for the Mavs' Saturday night home opener against the San Antonio Spurs and will be re-evaluated next week, per the team's announcement.

Flagg left Friday's game in the second quarter and didn't return. He went down after a hard foul from Pacers forward Aaron Nesmith, who appeared to hit Flagg in the back of the head and caused the Mavericks forward to land awkwardly.

The incident sparked a heated argument between Nesmith and Mavericks forward Naji Marshall, with Nesmith having to be separated from the group.

Nesmith was called for a flagrant foul after the contact, while both Nesmith and Marshall were given technical fouls for the incident.

Flagg hit both of his free throws awarded after Nesmith's flagrant, which occurred in the final minute of the half. He was subbed out afterward and headed into the locker room before halftime, grabbing at his left shoulder.

At the time he left, Flagg had racked up 14 points for the Mavericks in 17 minutes of play.

The Mavericks went on to get the 16-point victory over the Pacers behind 24 points from Kyrie Irving. Dallas led by as many as 37 points in the win.

articles.title: Former NBA Star Malik Beasley Negotiating Plea Deal over Gambling Charges
articles.summary: Former NBA player Malik Beasley is negotiating a plea agreement with the Department of Justice after initially pleading not guilty to charges that he altered his play in certain games in 2024 to enrich sports bettors and ease his own debts, his attorney said Saturday.
articles.body:
Former NBA player Malik Beasley is negotiating a plea agreement with the Department of Justice after initially pleading not guilty to charges that he altered his play in certain games in 2024 to enrich sports bettors and ease his own debts, his attorney said Saturday.

In July, Beasley entered a not guilty plea in New York federal court. He was among the latest big names caught up in a sweeping federal gambling investigation .

Beasley's attorney, Steve Haney, told The Associated Press in a text message that they were negotiating an agreement with the government "with an expected direction in the coming days."

Beasley, 29, and sports agent Paolo Zamorano, who has also pleaded not guilty, were among six people charged in an indictment unsealed this summer detailing a gambling scandal that has involved more than three dozen arrests.

Zamorano, 39, formerly represented another co-defendant, ex-NBA player Ed Davis, who had lent money to Beasley and is accused of acting as his "gatekeeper" in the alleged scheme.

Beasley is accused of fixing or trying to fix his performance in at least four games while playing for the Milwaukee Bucks in 2024 by under or overperforming bookmakers' expectations. In exchange, the indictment said, the bettors bribed Beasley — and his debts to Davis were reduced or eliminated.

"Only way you can beat Vegas is sports betting," Davis told Beasley in a Jan. 26, 2024, text message, according to the indictment. "Everything else they got the edge."

Beasley borrowed money from Davis, a former teammate, after racking up millions of dollars in gambling losses. His widely reported financial problems include disputes with a Detroit landlord, a Milwaukee barber and a Minnesota dentist. A 2025 lawsuit from a sports marketing agency resulted in a $1 million default judgment against him.

Beasley has been out of the NBA since playing with the Detroit Pistons in 2024-25 on a one-year, $6 million contract. He averaged 16 points per game and scored 20 in his last game, a playoff loss to the New York Knicks. He is one of five players in NBA history with more than 300 three-pointers in a season

articles.title: Dream, Valkyries stay off court for fourth WNBA Finals national anthem as some fans remain seated
articles.summary: Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries left the court before the national anthem for a fourth straight WNBA Finals game as Trump urged a boycott.
articles.body: The Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries were off the court for the national anthem before Saturday’s Game 4 of the WNBA Finals at State Farm Arena, marking their fourth straight absence in the series. Some fans also remained seated during the performance, including spectators who kept their hats on. I attempted to observe what Atlanta’s players do after leaving the court, but arena staff told me my credential did not grant access to that area and escorted me back to my assigned media seat. WNBA PLAYERS, COACHES REFUSE TO EXPLAIN NATIONAL ANTHEM ABSENCES AMID MOUNTING CRITICISM An employee inside State Farm Arena told OutKick that Dream players stand in a hallway after leaving the court before games. OutKick asked the Dream to confirm whether players remain there during the national anthem and explain what they do during the performance. The team did not immediately respond. Players from both teams said Friday that staying off the court during the anthem has been their practice for years. In the first three games, both teams left shortly before the anthem and returned seconds after it ended. Games 1 and 2 were played at Chase Center in San Francisco on Oct. 17 and 19. The series moved to Atlanta for Game 3 on Oct. 21. Atlanta entered Saturday with a 2–1 lead in the best-of-seven series after winning Wednesday’s Game 3, 97–71. The anthem absences have drawn criticism from President Donald Trump, who urged fans to stop watching the WNBA at an Oct. 22 rally in Iowa. Vice President JD Vance also called the absences "disgraceful." Atlanta coach Karl Smesko declined to explain the absences Atlanta coach Karl Smesko was asked Friday why his team left the floor for the anthem and whose decision that was. "We’re just kind of focused on the Finals," Smesko said. Asked whether he had any further comment about the anthem and his team’s absences on the league’s biggest stage, Smesko said, "No." An Atlanta public relations representative then moved to the next question. Rhyne Howard responds to Team USA criticism Dream guard Rhyne Howard was asked Friday about calls to exclude players from Team USA if they do not stand for the national anthem during the WNBA season. Riley Gaines and former Georgia state Rep. Vernon Jones have argued that anthem conduct should carry consequences when athletes seek to represent the United States internationally. "I don’t think I’ve been on the floor for the national anthem for any of my tenure in Atlanta, so if that’s what people are gonna look to nitpick for then so be it," Howard said. "But as far as competing for your team, when I go put on USA jersey I’m out for the national anthem every time, there’s no doubt about it." "Yes, I love the country that I play for and I love what we have here," she added. Howard and Dream teammate Angel Reese represented the United States at September’s FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup, where both stood for the anthem. Golden State had no players on that U.S. roster, although Valkyries head coach Natalie Nakase served as an assistant coach. OutKick followed up with Howard: "Is there a reason you’re not on the court for the anthem?" Howard and an Atlanta public relations representative both responded, "Next question." Natalie Nakase explains what she does during the anthem During Friday’s media availability in Atlanta, OutKick asked Nakase whose decision it was for Golden State to stay off the court and why. "We’re two years in," Nakase said. "That’s been part of our pregame." Asked again who decided and why, she said, "I really don’t know." "I understand your question," Nakase added. "I’m not trying to, you know, not answer your question. It’s just part of our pregame." OutKick followed up: "What do you do during those 90 seconds that you’re off the court?" "I’m with my staff, so I’m focused on my plays," Nakase said. Golden State’s public relations staff then moved to the next reporter. OutKick did not get an opportunity to ask why those preparations needed to happen during the anthem rather than before or afterward. Gabby Williams denies protest and cites a seven-year routine OutKick also asked Valkyries forward Gabby Williams whether the anthem absences are meant as a protest. "No," she said. Asked why the team was off the court, Williams responded: "That’s been the routine for like, seven years now." A Valkyries public relations representative then said, "Next question." Williams was born in Nevada, holds U.S. and French citizenship and represents France internationally. She joined Golden State this year after playing for Chicago from 2018–20 and Seattle from 2022–25. Williams’ reference to roughly seven years would reach back to her time in Chicago and span the three WNBA teams she has played for, though she did not explain whether each followed the same routine or how it began. There is a history of WNBA teams staying off the court as a demonstration. During the 2017 Finals, Los Angeles Sparks players voted to remain in the locker room in solidarity with Black Lives Matter, according to reporting at the time. Atlanta also published players’ union messaging in its Aug. 2, 2020, game notes. It said "the anthem does not represent freedom, justice and liberty for all Americans" and that players would "continue to protest" in various forms. Williams denied that the absences are a protest, but the pregame routine explanation still did not identify who established the practice or why it coincides with the anthem. WNBA rulebook and current enforcement remain separate questions The WNBA’s 2026 official rulebook says players, coaches and trainers are to "stand and line up in a dignified posture" along the sidelines or on the foul line during the national anthem. The Associated Press reported Oct. 20 that the league suspended its anthem protocols in 2017. The provision remains in the 2026 rulebook. OutKick has asked the WNBA to clarify its current requirements and enforcement, whether discipline is planned or under consideration, and whether teams have received instructions about being on the court. The league has not answered multiple requests for comment. Friday’s interviews were OutKick’s first opportunity to put the anthem questions directly to players and coaches. OutKick had attended all 13 formal press conferences during the first three Finals games without being called on. The emailed inquiries began after Game 1 on Oct. 17. OutKick followed up with the WNBA, Dream and Valkyries on Oct. 18 and again Oct. 20, asking about the absences, the teams’ plans for subsequent games and any league instructions. OutKick also contacted NBA Executive Vice President and Chief Communications Officer Mike Bass on Oct. 20. The inquiry asked about the NBA’s role in enforcing the WNBA provision, whether Commissioner Adam Silver or other NBA officials had discussed the absences with WNBA leadership, and possible exemptions or discipline. The WNBA, NBA and both teams’ front offices have not responded to OutKick’s repeated emailed requests for comment about the anthem absences. Friday’s responses came from players and coaches during media availabilities. And no one has given a good answer as to why.

articles.title: Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg has more to say about Lakers star Luka Doncic — ‘He’s not Michael Jordan’
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors rookie forward Yaxel Lendeborg doubled down on his criticism of Los Angeles Lakers superstar Luka Doncic on Saturday, declaring that he...
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors rookie forward Yaxel Lendeborg doubled down on his criticism of Los Angeles Lakers superstar Luka Doncic on Saturday, declaring that he is not afraid to confront the six-time All-Star because "he's not Michael Jordan."

Lendeborg addressed his ongoing exchange with Doncic during a locker room interview with Joseph Dycus of The Mercury News ahead of Golden State's Saturday night matchup against the Phoenix Suns.

"I'm not supposed to talk to him, something like that… He gonna say what he wanna say, I'm a say what I wanna say. I'm not afraid to talk to nobody, man. He's not Michael Jordan , like come on now," Lendeborg said with a laugh.

The 24-year-old rookie also acknowledged that his previous criticism of Doncic might have gone too far.

"It's fun trash talk. I feel like I did kinda take it overboard in the media, but you know it is what it is."

The exchange follows Lendeborg's comments after the Warriors suffered a 127-105 season-opening loss to the Lakers on Wednesday night.

Yaxel Lendeborg's Luka Doncic feud adds intrigue to Warriors-Lakers rematch

"I had a lot of respect for him [Luka Doncic], but being in there firsthand, watching all the whining and complaining, I lost all respect for him," Lendeborg said.

His latest remarks suggest that while he recognizes his initial comments might have been excessive, he remains unwilling to back down from the Lakers superstar.

The developing tension adds another storyline to the rivalry between the two Pacific Division opponents, who will meet again next week.

Meanwhile, Golden State enters Saturday's contest against Phoenix with an 0-2 record after falling 111-108 to the Memphis Grizzlies on Friday night.

articles.title: Celtics’ Jayson Tatum Fires Back at Jaylen Brown Drama With Shaq-Kobe Comparison
articles.summary: Jayson Tatum invokes childhood idol Kobe Bryant's famous rivalry with Shaq while addressing the growing Jaylen Brown controversy. The post Celtics’ Jayson Ta...
articles.body:
has heard enough about his supposed feud with Jaylen Brown. And the Boston Celtics star wants one thing made clear: Their breakup was nothing like the bitter ending to Shaquille O'Neal and Kobe Bryant's partnership with the Los Angeles Lakers.

After scoring 36 points in Boston's 107-103 victory over the New York Knicks on Friday, Tatum addressed speculation about his relationship with Brown, who was traded to the Philadelphia 76ers in July.

"This ain't no [expletive] Shaq and Kobe," Tatum said during his postgame news conference. "There's no beef."

His comments followed Brown's cryptic social media response to Tatum's account of learning about the blockbuster trade.

Jaylen Brown's Blue-Cap Comment Reignites Celtics Drama

In his Summer of Jayson video series , Tatum recalled being in Las Vegas when ESPN's Shams Charania informed him that Boston had traded Brown.

Tatum said Charania handed him a towel and warned him not to react.

"Put this over your face. Don't react. They just traded him," Tatum recalled.

When he learned Brown was headed to Philadelphia, Tatum couldn't believe it.

"You traded him down the street?" he asked.

However, Brown responded to an Instagram clip of the interview with a blue baseball cap emoji, commonly used to suggest someone is lying.

The reaction fueled questions about whether Brown believed Tatum knew more about the trade than he acknowledged.

Kobe Bryant's Biggest Fan Knows Shaq Feud's History

Tatum's comparison carries personal significance.

He grew up idolizing Bryant, collecting his jerseys and studying his game. In a 2018 interview with The Ringer , Tatum recalled telling his mother that he didn't simply want to play in the NBA .

Bryant later became a mentor, working out with Tatum during the Celtics forward's early NBA career.

That lifelong admiration gives Tatum a personal connection to one of basketball's most famous feuds.

Bryant and O'Neal won three consecutive championships with the Lakers from 2000 through 2002. Yet their partnership deteriorated amid public disagreements over leadership, playing styles and their respective roles.

Los Angeles eventually traded O'Neal to Miami in 2004.

However, the former teammates reconciled years later. During a 2015 podcast conversation , both acknowledged their past disagreements and expressed mutual respect.

Their relationship improved further before Bryant died in 2020.

Unlike that prolonged public conflict, Tatum insists his separation from Brown wasn't driven by personal animosity.

Tatum Wants Celtics Championship Legacy Remembered

Boston's breakup came through a front-office decision to trade Brown for Paul George and draft compensation.

Together, Tatum and Brown reached two NBA Finals and won the 2024 championship, with Brown earning Finals MVP honors.

"All of y'all kind of saw us grow up and everything that we accomplished," Tatum said. "It should be celebrated."

He acknowledged that Brown has every right to his feelings about the trade.

"Everybody is entitled to their own feelings," Tatum said.

Still, he would rather discuss their relationship privately than let speculation overshadow their accomplishments.

Tatum said he called and texted Brown after learning of the trade.

For a player who grew up watching the Shaq-Kobe rivalry unfold and later developed a relationship with Bryant, the distinction matters.

The Lakers stars needed years to mend their relationship. Tatum believes his partnership with Brown deserves to be remembered for what they accomplished together, not an assumed feud.

articles.summary: There was a time, not too long ago, when the Milwaukee Bucks playing against whatever team LeBron James played for was nationally televised. Indeed, watching...
articles.body:
There was a time, not too long ago, when the Milwaukee Bucks playing against whatever team LeBron James played for was nationally televised. Indeed, watching the NBA's all-time leading scorer take on Giannis and the Bucks always made for an entertaining matchup.

Unfortunately, times change. Giannis now plays for the Miami Heat, the Bucks are in the beginning stages of a rebuild, and LeBron is in his 24th season in the NBA and playing for the Philadelphia 76ers.

However, he will not be playing against Milwaukee on Saturday night.

The Milwaukee Bucks will not face LeBron James on Saturday

Due to the fact that the Milwaukee Brewers are in their first World Series in 44 years, the Bucks have understandably taken a backseat to the city's baseball team. Given the fact that they are in a rebuild and Giannis gone, not many fans have much interest in the team anyway.

That being said, the Bucks organization has embraced their new identity. They moved their home opener, originally scheduled for Friday night, to Friday afternoon. What is more, several Bucks players, and head coach Taylor Jenkins, went to Game One of the World Series to support the Brewers.

Soon after, Milwaukee's NBA team flew out to Philadelphia where they will face the 76ers on Saturday night. However, they will not be facing LeBron:

Milwaukee, 0-2, is looking for their first win of the season after falling to the Chicago Bulls 132-125 on Friday night. Philadelphia, meanwhile, is 2-0 and begins the first night of a back-to-back when they face the Bucks.

LeBron is averaging 15.5 points, 9.5 rebounds, and 6.0 assists per game through his first two games in a 76ers uniform.

The Bucks have a clean injury report with all 15 rostered players available.

articles.title: New York Knicks employees to get NBA championship rings after admitting to phishing email 'mistake'
articles.summary: A Madison Square Garden (MSG) spokesperson admitted that "using the rings as a lure to gain employees attention was an unfortunate mistake", before adding that more than 275 employees were already set to be gifted rings "in about 4-6 weeks", worth more than $3.7 million
articles.body:
The Athletic reported on Thursday that some employees received an email in September that said: "Your Employee Championship Ring is here". But those who clicked on the link in the email were informed that they had failed a phishing test and would have to attend a mandatory cybersecurity class.

A Madison Square Garden (MSG) spokesperson admitted on Friday that "using the rings as a lure to gain employees attention was an unfortunate mistake".

In a further statement on Saturday, MSG conceded that using an email regarding the selection of rings to train staffers about cybersecurity was a mistake, though "reminding our employees to protect our IP was not".

Having secured the Knicks' first title since 1973 last season, players were awarded their rings on Tuesday night before losing their season opener against LeBron James' Philadelphia 76ers.

MSG added that more than 275 employees were already set to be gifted rings "in about 4-6 weeks", worth more than $3.7 million.

"There is a great deal of misinformation regarding the championship rings," the statement clarified. "The plan has always been to distribute more than 275 rings and jewelry to the people in the organization who were part of last season's success."

articles.standfirst: El catalán es el único equipo que no conoce la victoria en cinco partidos en la Liga Endesa
articles.summary: El catalán es el único equipo que no conoce la victoria en cinco partidos en la Liga Endesa
articles.body: El Recoletas Salud San Pablo Burgos brilló este sábado en el Nou Congost, donde ganó con contundencia a un Kids&Us Manresa que sigue sin conocer la victoria por 81-99 en un duelo dominado de principio a fin por el equipo dirigido por Porfi Fisac. El base Chase Audige, con 21 puntos anotados, fue pieza clave para que su equipo ganara con tanto dominio en una de las pistas más difíciles de la Liga Endesa. Los burgaleses comenzaron el partido mucho más entonados en ataque, lo que provocó un primer parcial a favor con 10 puntos casi seguidos de Sekou Doumbouya que hicieron encender todas las alarmas del Nou Congost (8-15, min. 5). El Kids&Us Manresa, lejos de reaccionar tras el primer tiempo muerto, vio como el San Pablo Burgos siguió muy acertado, esta vez gracias a la muñeca de Chase Audige, que fue un auténtico dolor de cabeza para la defensa local (16-27, min. 8). Y el parcial no se quedó aquí, ya que los visitantes anotaron en la última jugada en transición con una bandeja de Dusan Radosavljevic para poner el 20-34 al final del primer cuarto. El guión no cambió en el segundo, con un San Pablo Burgos muy sólido en ambos lados de la pista en el que Dani Díez, en una jugada de mucho poderío interior, puso el +16 en el luminoso (29-45, min. 15). Los catalanes lograron rebajar un poco la desventaja, pero de nuevo se toparon con la mano de Audige para que los castellanoleoneses mantuvieran una buena ventaja (37-50, min. 18). En los últimos dos minutos de la primera mitad no hubo apenas canastas, tan sólo una visitante, y el equipo de Porfi Fisac se marchó a los vestuarios con un 37-52 que no gustó nada a la afición local. En la reanudación, los burgaleses llegaron a ponerse con un +18 en un abrir y cerrar de ojos, pero el buen hacer en la pintura de Nick Ongenda en los catalanes hizo que el marcador se apretara un poco más dentro de la gran ventaja que ya tenían los visitantes (43-58, min. 23). Sin embargo, cuando parecía que el Kids&Us Manresa podría rebajar la barrera psicológica de los diez puntos de desventaja, el San Pablo metió la sexta marcha de la mano de Christian Sengfelder para irse hasta el +20 (54-74, min. 28). En el tramo final del tercer cuarto hubo un intercambio de canastas que dejó a los burgaleses con un 63-81 a favor antes de encarar los últimos diez minutos de choque. Con el encuentro prácticamente sentenciado, el Kids&Us Manresa tiró de orgullo para rebajar la desventaja lo antes posible, y el descaro del joven Gerard Fernández hizo creer al Nou Congost en una más que difícil remontada (69-84, min. 34). Los del Bages intentaron meter el miedo en el cuerpo a los visitantes, pero un triple a tabla sobre la bocina de posesión de Radosavljevic sentenció definitivamente el encuentro (72-90, min. 37). Al final, el San Pablo Burgos venció por 81-99 al Kids&Us Manresa para sumar el segundo triunfo de la temporada en la Liga Endesa, mientras que los catalanes seguirán como colistas y único equipo sin victorias en este inicio de temporada. 81.
